label: prf:binding-genfun-qdifference
title: Proof of the q-difference recurrence of the binding generating function
html:
Write G(x;q)=\sum_{n\geq 0}B_n x^n and, for polynomial R, R(q,x)=\sum_{j=0}^{d} r_j(q)\,x^{j}. The coefficient of x^{n} in G(qx;q) is q^{n}B_{n}, and in R(q,x)G(x;q) it is \sum_{j=0}^{d} r_j B_{n-j}. Hence

  (q^{n} - r_0)\,B_{n} \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{d} r_j\,B_{n-j},

and for q^n \neq r_0 this solves for B_n in terms of B_{n-1},\dots,B_{n-d} with coefficients r_j/(q^n - r_0), rational in q and q^n. A Laurent R shifts the indices but leaves the factor q^n on the B_n coefficient. This is the standard fact that a q-holonomic series has q-recursive coefficients; it fixes every term from R and the first d terms. (Note that the factor q^n makes the recurrence coefficients r_j/(q^n - r_0) depend explicitly on the index n, rather than being constant in n.)

For the Archimedean image, apply \tau at q=q_0 and let q\to q_0 act on the shift operator x\mapsto qx: the multiplicative q-shift degenerates to the infinitesimal generator x\,\partial_x (the confluent limit of a q-difference operator), so G(qx;q)=R(q,x)G(x;q) passes to a linear differential equation x\,\partial_x \widehat{G} = \rho(x)\,\widehat{G} on the realised \widehat{G}=\tau G — the Dirac-type equation. Given the depth-d recurrence, with position-dependent coefficients, the term identity follows; the existence of R for the binding G is the conjectural input (carried as a hypothesis). \qquad\blacksquare
